claims.text: Failure modes: the multi-account file passes, 27 tests including the two added here. One checks that pairing does not depend on the order the accounts are imported in. The other checks that a protected credit (a lending drawdown) is never paired.
Full suite and lint pass at 508290f. Lint was re-run after the two new tests (commit 90d4969).
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q -x ; ruff check src tests

claims.text: Idempotency: importing the same file again into a two-account case changes nothing. An import refused at the combined limit writes no log entry, no statement and no input file, so the case is left as the next run expects.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest tests/test_multi_account.py -q -k 'reimport or refused_combined_import or import_refused'
claims.proof_output: covered by the 27 passed above: test_reimport_in_two_account_case_changes_nothing, test_refused_combined_import_leaves_no_input_file, test_import_refused_at_combined_limit, test_import_refused_when_an_account_cannot_be_read_for_the_limit

claims.text: Authz: there is one new entry point, the combined figures at /lines?account=*. It refuses a request with no token or a wrong token (403, no line ids in the body). An override against the combined key '*' is refused and records nothing.

Migration and rollback: there is no stored-data change. The combined figures and the pairing are computed from the case's inputs, and nothing new is written to the case log or the evidence beyond what was there. A case with one account takes no new path: pair_own_accounts returns [] and combined_figures returns None. Rolling back means reinstalling the previous package; there is nothing to repair.

Performance (R52): on a 10,000-line case of two 5,000-line accounts, case_figures plus combined_figures took 1.2 s with an override on the warm path, and case_summary took 1.67 s. The first cold call took 2.79 s, which includes loading the ruleset. Pairing indexes credits by pence, so it does no N+1 scan.
claims.proof_cmd: PYTHONPATH=src python <scratchpad>/probe.py  (2 x _big(5000) from tests/test_workspace_overrides.py, different seeds)
claims.proof_output: no override 2.79 / paired lines 4 groups 0 / with override 1.2 / summary 1.67

claims.text: Observability: each paired line records its provenance as rule_id 'pairing:<account>:<line id>', naming its other half. That record is how anyone can see the pairing ran. Unpaired candidates appear in the judgement queue as possible_own_account_transfer, with pairs_with.
Security, input: no new dependency, secret or query interpolation. Account keys refuse ':' and '*', so a prefixed case line id cannot collide with another line's id.

notes: Gaps for the owner, none fixed in code because each needs a design decision. (1) R8 says the pairing window is 'within the configured days', but PAIRING_DAYS = 3 is a code constant that firm.yaml and indicators.yaml do not expose. Making it configurable needs a decision on which file holds it and whether its hash goes into the snapshot. (2) Pairing ranks above unprotected verdicts (C1 precedence step 3). So a supplier debit in one account and a trading credit of the same amount within 3 days in another (for example a card settlement) become own-account transfers and leave M2 without any warning. Design intends this, and it can only lower M2, but no indicator flags it; the owner may want a test or an indicator. (3) No alert or log line exists beyond provenance. That matches the local-only design, which has no remote alerting. (4) Docs: README:189 names the pairing in the precedence, but it documents neither the 'pairing:<account>:<id>' rule form nor the 'All accounts' workspace section. The design's Line provenance section should add the pairing form. (5) The R52 timing is a probe, not a runner tier. The existing R52 tests cover only one-account cases.
